text:
anya: Heads up — saw a ~300ms p99 tail spike on the us-east serving cluster between 09:10–09:25 UTC. Affects /generate (r3) and /chat (r1). Error rates low but latency SLOs tripped. This started after yesterday's runtime change to admission thresholds. Anyone digging?

perf-bot: ALERT: latency_spike detected (us-east). p95: 120ms -> 420ms, p99: 280ms -> 610ms. Related deploy: commit f3a2b (scheduler/admission) by jamal.

kevin: grabbing traces now. Any chance this is noisy neighbor or a scheduling regression vs kernel selection?

anya: we ruled out noisy nodes — infra shows normal GPU util and no OOMs. Throughput dropped ~15% on affected machines.

sophie: uploading quick profiler dump. pprof shows a jump in time spent in `matmul_generic` for requests with seq_len > 800. Kernel selection logs indicate fallback to generic kernel for certain model shards around 09:08. Suspect kernel picker heuristic changed behavior when microbatch sizes changed.

sophie: snippet from runtime logs:

```
[09:07:58] kernel_picker: model=redwood-xl-8k shard=3 estimated_seq=1024 fallback_threshold=0.67
[09:08:01] kernel_picker: selected=matmul_generic (cost_est=1.23) note="fallback from optimized_matmul_v2"
[09:08:02] kv_cache: hit_rate=0.81 avg_kv_latency=1.9ms
[09:08:05] scheduler: microbatch_size=4 admitted=37 queued=12
```

kevin: interesting — admission saw more small microbatches (size 2-4) after change. That increases scheduling overhead and decreases amortization for optimized kernels that benefit from larger contiguous token work.

jamal: i pushed the admission tweak yesterday to lower max_wait_ms to improve latency for short requests. config diff:

```
- scheduler.max_microbatch_wait_ms: 8
+ scheduler.max_microbatch_wait_ms: 4  # reduce tail for small requests
- scheduler.admit_if_util_below: 0.85
+ scheduler.admit_if_util_below: 0.9
```

jamal: goal was better p95 for short requests, but looks like it created more tiny microbatches and changed kernel selection thresholds due to different seq distributions hitting shards.

anya: any quick repro on staging? can we flip the admit change or tweak kernel-picker to avoid fallback?

sophie: ran a staged replay with the change and reproduced the p99 bump. If we increase microbatch target to 8 or adjust the kernel picker to prefer optimized_matmul_v2 when estimated_total_tokens > 4096, tail drops back to baseline in replay.

kevin: propose immediate mitigation: revert max_microbatch_wait_ms to 8 in us-east, and add a conservative kernel-picker override for the next 24h. Then schedule a proper rollout after more testing.

jamal: will open a rollback PR now and add a runtime flag `kernel_picker.force_prefer_v2=true` for canary.

perf-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0427. Priority: P2. Owners: eng-runtime@, eng-sre@.

anya: thanks. After rollback, please monitor p95/p99 and KV cache behavior — I want to verify no regressions to hit-rate or token cost. Also capture a detailed profile for a few long requests to check that KV cache reuse isn't being invalidated by microbatch ordering.

sophie: noted — I'll also add a small patch to kernel-picker metrics to expose why fallback decisions happen (cost_est, shard_load, microbatch_size) so we can correlate in future.

kevin: assigning follow-ups: jamal rollback + patch (1h), sophie deeper profiling + metrics (2h), anya continue monitoring + event postmortem stub.

anya: ping me when rollback is live and I’ll validate in the dashboard. :thumbsup:

jamal: PR submitted: https://git.company/redwood/runtime/pull/1452 — rolling back wait_ms and adding canary flag. Deploying to canary first.

sophie: uploaded profiler traces to internal bucket: s3://redwood-dev/perf/1780146789/ — saved pprof and scheduler histograms.

kevin: good work team. We'll follow up with a short postmortem once metrics settle.

anya: thanks everyone — keeping this thread as the single source for timeline + actions.
